Bug_Details:
Use Random.nextInt(int).  Random.nextInt() % n can have negative results Random.nextInt() % n has a 1/n chance of being 0
a 1/2n chance of being each number from 1 to n-1 inclusive
a 1/2n chance of being each number from -1 to -(n-1) inclusive Many users expect a uniformly distributed random integer between 0 and n-1
inclusive, but you must use random.nextInt(n) to get that behavior. If the
original behavior is truly desired, use (random.nextBoolean() ? 1 : -1) *
random.nextInt(n).
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the code by using the modulo operator (%) to obtain a random integer between 0 and n-1 inclusive. The modulo operator can produce negative results, which is not what the user expects when using Random.nextInt(n) to generate a random integer between 0 and n-1 inclusive.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by using the `Random.nextInt(int)` method with a modulo operation. This causes the result to be negative with a probability of 1/2n.
